excluded.reason: Copyrighted 1960, renewed 1988 by Sociedades Biblicas Unidas, and a registered trademark. The rights holder names mobile applications and websites as requiring written permission. Never distributable without a licence.

Robinson's Morphological Analysis Codes as distributed by CrossWire are CC BY-SA 3.0. The share-alike obligation propagates to derived data, which would taint every catalog it entered. The underlying coding scheme is a fact, but the distributed file is a 2002 copyrighted compilation.

The Open Scriptures Strong's dictionary data file is GPL-3.0 — a copyleft software licence applied to data. Using it in a closed app would arguably trigger GPL obligations. Strong's 1890 is public domain and is re-derived from the archival scan instead.
Robertson's Word Pictures volumes 5 and 6 were published in 1932/1933 and renewed in 1960. Under the 95-years-from-publication rule they are not US public domain until 2028 and 2029 respectively.

Vine's Expository Dictionary (1940) is genuinely contested: probably public domain by 2026, but with no authoritative statement confirming non-renewal and an unresolved public debate. Excluded pending legal confirmation.
The common modern edition of the Scofield Reference Notes carries substantive 1970s additions by Palmore/Royalston and is copyrighted, despite the 1917 original being old.

The Spanish Matthew Henry in circulation is Francisco Lacueva's CLIE translation (1983), a modern copyrighted work. Biblioteca de Autores Cristianos republishes ancient authors in modern copyrighted translations. There is no public-domain Spanish commentary available.
Tyndale House STEP Bible publishes its own datasets under CC BY-NC 3.0, which forbids commercial use.
Liddell & Scott & Jones, 9th edition (1940) is in copyright; the Perseus electronic edition is CC BY-SA.

The CrossWire module SpaRV1909 is not the text this catalog ships, and the difference matters. The module's own notice says 'El texto de la Reina-Valera 1909 es de dominio publico' but that the Strong's-number labels were added by Ruben Gomez, and CrossWire classifies the distribution as 'Copyrighted; Permission to distribute granted to CrossWire'. The text is clean; the tagging is not. The Strong's edition is therefore excluded while the untagged 1909 text ships. Note also that the module is SWORD zText, not USFM, so the existing build could not read it without a second format reader.

Biblica Open Nueva Biblia Viva 2008 (spaonbv), CC BY-SA 4.0. Share-alike is contagious across derived data, so folding it into a closed commercial catalog would impose the obligation on the catalog itself. The same reasoning that excludes Robinson's morphological codes. It does have USFM available, so the blocker is the licence and nothing else.

Santa Biblia Valera 1602 Purificada (spav1602p). The 1602 text underneath is public domain by age, but the 'Purificada' edition of 2007/2019/2024 is not: its notice reserves all rights and explicitly prohibits adding, removing or altering any letter, word or punctuation mark. A digitised Bible with a prohibition on modification cannot be the input to a build that strips markers and rewrites encoding. USFM is available, so the blocker is the edition's terms, not the format.

Felipe Scio de San Miguel, Nuevo Testamento (1797), public domain and historically significant as the first Spanish New Testament from the Commission of Toledo. Excluded from this build for a content reason rather than a licence one: it is a translation of the Latin Vulgate, not of the Hebrew and Greek, and it covers 27 of the 66 books. Worth revisiting for the Catholic canon, which the current catalog cannot otherwise fill in Spanish.

Reina-Valera 1865 is public domain and its USFM exists under CC0, and it was built during this work as the control for the 1909 build. It is not shipped because 1909 is the superior revision of the same lineage and the two are not additive: shipping both would give the library two near-identical Spanish texts and no reason to prefer either. Kept as a recorded alternative if 1909 is ever withdrawn.

license.attribution: Reina-Valera 1909. Cross-references: Treasury of Scripture Knowledge (public domain), redistributed by CrossReferences.org under CC BY 4.0.
license.basis: The 1909 revision of Casiodoro de Reina (1569) and Cipriano de Valera (1602), collated by the Sociedad Biblica de Madrid against the Hebrew and Greek. Public domain by age: 1909, pre-1931 in the United States, and every named translator long deceased for life+70. The USFM transcription used for the build is published under CC0 by palabra-de-dios, which is the most permissive dedication available and carries no share-alike or attribution obligation. Chosen over the other freely redistributable Spanish texts because it is the revision the Spanish scholarly tradition actually cites; RV1960, the descendant in wide use today, is copyrighted and trademarked and is recorded in `excluded`. Source completeness: the USFM declares 31,102 verses and supplies the text of 31,084. The 18 absent are \v markers with a number and no body, listed here in full so that each can be checked individually: Job 35:16; Job 38:39; Job 38:40; Job 38:41; Job 40:20; Job 40:21; Job 40:22; Job 40:23; Job 40:24; Números 12:16; Números 29:40; 1 Samuel 23:29; 2 Samuel 20:26; 2 Crónicas 33:25; Oseas 11:12; Jonás 1:17; Hechos 19:41; 2 Corintios 13:14. They are absent from the module rather than filled, because an empty row renders as a verse that says nothing and reusing the previous verse would invent scripture. Every build prints this set and the count, so a hole cannot quietly widen; test/catalog_reproducibility_test.dart asserts the list.

license.basis: Juan Straubinger (1883-1956). Life+70 under Ley 17.336 art. 10 (Chile), Spain and the EU expires 2026-12-31, so the work enters the public domain on 2027-01-01. NOT public domain in the United States, where the 95-years-from-publication rule for works of 1931-1977 runs to 2043. Textual verification is required before distribution.
